relationships.subject: capsaicin
relationships.evidence_quote: Capsaicin, the main bioactive pungent compound in chili peppers, interacts with TRPV1, leading to cellular calcium influx and depolarization

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: the activation of TRPV1 in the tumor microenvironment of Lewis lung carcinoma triggers the release of CGRP from sensory neurons

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: capsaicin-induced TRPV1 activation triggers apoptosis in colorectal cancer cells through the calcineurin–NFAT2–p53 signaling pathway

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: blocking TRPV1 can inhibit hyperthermia-induced calcium influx, which in turn suppresses heat shock protein (HSP70) overexpression by preventing HSF1 from translocating to the nucleus

key_findings: Review: TRPV1 has a dual role in cancer, acting as tumor suppressor or promoter depending on context, and capsaicin-TRPV1 signaling induces apoptosis and chemosensitization.
TRPV1-CGRP signaling from sensory neurons promotes tumor angiogenesis via VEGF and suppresses antitumor immunity.
